channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: US War Commission Meets Pakistan Army Chief on Afghanistan Conflict Role
item.description: A US Afghanistan War Commission delegation met Pakistan's army chief, Asim Munir, to discuss Pakistan's role in the Afghanistan conflict. Discussions covered regional security and developments in Afghanistan, with the commission examining US engagement. Munir presented Pakistan's perspective on security dynamics and challenges.

item.title: Kazakhstan Developing Digital Map of Agricultural Land Quality
item.description: Kazakhstan is creating an information system for land resource management, including a digital map of agricultural land quality. This system will integrate data on soil quality, cadastral information, and infrastructure to support rational fertilizer application. The digitization of all agricultural lands is complete.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Joint Production and Value Chains in Berlin
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed to Berlin the creation of joint production and value chains. Kazakhstan produces 21 out of 34 raw materials of strategic importance to the European economy. He emphasized the strong strategic partnership between Kazakhstan and Germany over thirty years.

item.title: Over 200 Million Som Unjustly Charged to Patients to be Returned in Uzbekistan
item.description: Over 200 million Uzbek som, unjustly collected from citizens, will be returned by medical facilities in Namangan, Samarkand, and Navoi regions. The Committee for the Protection of Competition initiated proceedings following the overcharging of patients.

item.title: Kazakh Prime Minister Orders Measures to Prevent Vegetable Shortages and Price Hikes
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov instructed regional administrations to secure supplies of socially significant vegetables and prevent shortages or price increases during the off-season. He emphasized the importance of subsidies for crop development and timely harvesting, acknowledging challenges from drought but noting expectations of above-average yields and high grain quality.

item.title: US Secretary of State: Foreign Actor Involved in Fafard Air Base Security Incident
item.description: The US Secretary of State stated that a foreign actor was involved in the security incident at the Fafard Air Base. Further details regarding the nature of the incident or the identity of the foreign actor were not provided in the source text.

item.title: Kazakh Prime Minister Orders Measures to Prevent Winter Vegetable Price Hikes
item.description: Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed regional authorities to prevent shortages and price gouging of vegetables during the off-season. He emphasized the importance of forming winter and spring reserves, particularly for potatoes, and ensuring timely procurement and storage. The government also aims to support farmers in finding export markets for surplus produce.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Agriculture Ministry Projects Grain Harvest of Around 23 Million Tons This Year
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Agriculture anticipates a grain harvest of approximately 23 million tons this year. This projection is higher than the average annual yield of 18-19 million tons but lower than the record harvests of the past two years. The ministry reports that nearly all grain and oilseed crops are in good or satisfactory condition.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims for 23 Million Tons of Grain by 2026, Exceeding Average Yields
item.description: Kazakhstan expects to harvest around 23 million tons of grain by 2026, a figure higher than the average annual yield of 18-19 million tons but below last year's record. The Ministry of Agriculture stated that approximately 20 million tons have already been harvested, with 83% of the campaign complete. Challenging weather conditions are forecast for key grain-producing regions.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Constitutional Court Overturns Rule Allowing Detention Up to 10 Days Without Court Sanction
item.description: Uzbekistan's Constitutional Court has ruled that a provision allowing detention of up to 10 days without judicial sanction violates the constitution. The court affirmed that individuals cannot be held for more than 48 hours without a court order. The ruling, effective September 25, addresses complaints about illegal administrative detentions exceeding 48 hours.

item.title: Heating systems activated in five regions of Kazakhstan
item.description: Heating systems have been launched in five regions of Kazakhstan: Pavlodar, Akmola, North Kazakhstan, East Kazakhstan, and Kostanay. The Vice Minister of Energy stated that heating will be provided to central, western, and eastern regions by the weekend. Preparations include 4.9 million tons of coal and 127,000 tons of mazut.

item.title: Tajik bank stops servicing Russian citizens' cards
item.description: A commercial bank in Tajikistan has notified clients that it will stop servicing Russian citizens' cards from October. Customers report difficulties withdrawing funds. The bank cited protection against fraudulent operations and requires biometric identification in person by September 30 for continued service.

item.title: Kazakhstan's harvest campaign enters final stage
item.description: Kazakhstan's grain harvest campaign is in its final stages, with some regions completing their work. The Vice Minister of Agriculture reported that over 95% of areas have been harvested in several key regions. The campaign is proceeding in an organized manner, utilizing 130,000 tractors and 29,000 combine harvesters.

item.title: Crime in Kyrgyzstan Rises 7.3% in First Eight Months of 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan registered 24,839 crimes in the first eight months of 2026, a 7.3% increase from the previous year. While overall crime growth slowed, property crimes rose 11.8%, driven by a 1.5-fold increase in fraud cases. The National Statistical Committee reported these figures, citing the Prosecutor General's Office.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Up to 5 Years Imprisonment for Unauthorized Apartment Building Construction
item.description: Uzbekistan is strengthening penalties for constructing apartment buildings without a permit from the Construction Inspectorate. Violators face fines of up to 450 base calculation amounts. Repeat offenses after administrative penalties can lead to 3 to 5 years imprisonment. The law takes effect in late December 2026.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Agriculture Ministry: No Basis for Beef Price Surge
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice Minister of Agriculture stated there is no basis for a significant increase in beef prices. The domestic market is fully supplied by local production, which has increased this year. Cattle numbers are also growing, according to the ministry.

item.title: Kazakhstan Uncovers Scheme Falsifying Foreign Grain as Domestic
item.description: Financial Monitoring Agency in Kazakhstan's West Kazakhstan region uncovered a scheme involving the illegal import of approximately 130,000 tons of foreign grain, valued at 11.2 billion tenge. The grain was disguised as Kazakh produce using fictitious companies and contracts to obtain preferential domestic rail tariffs for export.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Agriculture Ministry sees no grounds for sharp beef price increase
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Agriculture does not anticipate a sharp rise in beef prices, according to Vice Minister Nazgul Khatepova. She stated that the domestic market is fully supplied by local production, with average beef prices around 3,800 tenge per kilogram. Production volumes are also increasing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP proposes separate ministry for water resources
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan has proposed creating a separate ministry for water resources and land reclamation. The MP argued that water supply and irrigation issues require independent solutions and are strategically linked to energy. The current ministry believes water resources and agriculture are inseparable.

item.title: UAE President and Turkish Foreign Minister Discuss Regional Stability Efforts
item.description: UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan met with Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan to discuss efforts promoting regional stability and peace. The meeting, reported by WAM, focused on Middle Eastern developments and security. Discussions also touched upon intensified efforts to resolve tensions between Iran and the United States.

item.title: Uzbek MP Argues Death Penalty for Pedophiles Poses Risk to Children
item.description: Uzbekistan's parliament is considering a bill to toughen penalties for sexual violence against children. MP Bobur Bekmurodov opposes the death penalty for pedophiles, arguing it could create risks for children if perpetrators demand specific conditions. He advocates for life imprisonment instead.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Build and Repair 13 Reservoirs by Year-End
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to construct and renovate 13 reservoirs by the end of the year. This was announced during a meeting of the committee on international affairs, defense, security, and migration.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Grain Exports Increase to Central Asia, China, and Afghanistan
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Transport Minister Zhanibek Taizhanov reported that 9.3 million tons of grain were transported by rail in the first eight months of the year, a 13% increase from last year. Exports to Central Asia rose 37%, to China by 34%, and to Afghanistan by 4.4 times, reaching 655,000 tons.

item.title: Over 150 Human Rights Defenders Urge Kazakhstan Not to Extradite Individuals to Russia
item.description: More than 150 human rights defenders have called on Kazakhstan not to extradite Yemelyanova and Movlaev to Russia. The appeal highlights concerns regarding the potential extradition of individuals to face charges.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Future Increasingly Shaped by Urban Centers, Says UNDP Official
item.description: Uzbekistan's urbanization rate has reached 54.5%, with Tashkent at 100% and Khorezm below 40%. A UNDP official notes that cities are becoming crucial centers for transformation, facing complex challenges from economic instability to climate pressure, but also potential solutions.

item.title: Energy Ministry Promises Completion of Semey Heating Network Repairs Soon
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy has pledged to complete repairs on Semey's heating networks in the near future. Reconstruction of three main heating lines in Petropavlovsk is finished, and work on other regional networks is progressing, with some connections already made.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Up to 5 Years Imprisonment for Unauthorized Resale of Apartments
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced amendments to its construction sector regulations, establishing a penalty of up to five years in prison for the unauthorized resale of apartments in multi-story buildings. This measure aims to improve state control and management in the construction industry.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Agriculture sees no grounds for sharp meat price hikes
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Agriculture does not anticipate a sharp increase in beef prices. The average price nationwide is around 3,800 tenge per kilogram, though some Astana markets sell it for up to 4,500 tenge. The ministry cites sufficient domestic production and growing livestock numbers as reasons against a significant price surge.

item.title: Kazakhstan allocates additional 41.3 thousand tons of diesel for grain drying
item.description: Kazakhstan has allocated an additional 41.3 thousand tons of diesel fuel for drying grain, considering the rainy harvest season. A total of 401 thousand tons of diesel was initially allocated for the harvest campaign, with 67% already delivered. State support measures have helped reduce the wear of agricultural machinery.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Germany to Establish Joint Water Hub for Technology and Projects
item.description: Kazakhstan and Germany plan to create a joint water hub for technology exchange, digital solutions, and collaborative projects. The initiative aims to elevate cooperation in water resource management between the two nations. The proposal was presented at a roundtable in Berlin focused on strategic water partnership.

item.title: Constitutional Court Overturns Rule Allowing Detention Up to 10 Days Without Court Order
item.description: Uzbekistan's Constitutional Court has declared unconstitutional a rule allowing detention for up to 10 days without a court order for border crossing violations. The ruling, effective September 25, found the norm to be in violation of the constitution after complaints of illegal detentions were investigated.

item.title: President's directives shape state policy and citizen life
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's directives are being implemented through laws and government resolutions, addressing key societal issues. Expert analysis suggests these directives, when codified, yield concrete results, impacting everything from economic priorities to social welfare and infrastructure development.

item.title: Putin Bans Publication of Russian Oil Refinery Operations and Fuel Production Data
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has signed a decree restricting the publication of information related to the fuel and energy sector. Data on fuel processing and production volumes at oil refineries, as well as sales and transportation routes for gasoline and diesel, will now be classified.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Agriculture Ministry Sees No Grounds for Sharp Beef Price Increase
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Agriculture stated there are no reasons for a significant rise in beef prices, as the domestic market is fully supplied by local production. The average price for beef is around 3,800 tenge per kilogram, with production volumes and livestock numbers increasing.

item.title: Tajikistan's Prime Minister Meets with ITU Telecommunication Development Bureau Director
item.description: On September 28, 2026, Tajikistan's Prime Minister Kohir Rasulzada met with Kosmas Zavazava, Director of the ITU's Telecommunication Development Bureau. They discussed expanding cooperation in digitalization and digital technologies. Rasulzada highlighted Tajikistan's 32-year membership in the ITU and its initiative on AI for sustainable development in Central Asia.

item.title: Tajikistan Outlines Regional Economic Cooperation Priorities in Ulaanbaatar
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Economic Development and Trade participated in a development partners dialogue in Ulaanbaatar, focusing on trade facilitation, tourism, and regional competitiveness. He emphasized regional economic cooperation and connectivity, highlighting achievements in simplifying trade procedures, developing infrastructure, and improving standards. Digitalization and SME involvement were stressed for Central Asia.

item.title: US and Saudi Foreign Ministers Discuss Regional Security, Including Iran and Yemen
item.description: US Secretary of State Antony Blinken met with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan to discuss bilateral cooperation on regional security and stability. Key topics included Iran, Gaza, Sudan, and Yemen. The meeting occurred amid heightened tensions between the US and Iran, and intensified fighting involving the Houthi movement in Yemen.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Medical Facilities Overcharged Patients Nearly 125 Million Som
item.description: Uzbekistan's Antimonopoly Committee found that three medical facilities in Namangan, Samarkand, and Navoi regions violated pricing regulations for paid services, overcharging citizens by nearly 125 million som. Specific instances include the Namangan regional children's multidisciplinary medical center charging 34.3 million som for unjustified ultrasound services and the Kattakorgan district health department overcharging 55.7 million som.

item.title: UN agency warns funding crisis may leave 8.3 million displaced people without aid
item.description: The UN refugee agency warns a deepening funding crisis could leave 8.3 million displaced people without assistance and push protection systems towards collapse. Facing a $5.789 billion gap, UNHCR received only 32% of required funds by July, while the number of displaced people nears record levels.

item.title: Uzbek President Awards Educators and Mentors on Professional Holiday
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has honored a group of educators and mentors with honorary titles, orders, and medals for their outstanding contributions to the education and upbringing system. The awards were presented on the occasion of the Teacher and Mentor Day.
